an3.29:1.1: “Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world.
an3.29:1.3: The blind person, the one-eyed person, and the two-eyed person.
an3.29:1.4: (1) “And what, bhikkhus, is the blind person?
an3.29:1.5: Here, some person lacks the kind of eye with which one can acquire wealth not yet acquired and increase wealth already acquired,
an3.29:1.6: and he also lacks the kind of eye with which one can know wholesome and unwholesome qualities, blameworthy and blameless qualities, inferior and superior qualities, dark and bright qualities with their counterparts.
an3.29:1.7: This is called the blind person.
an3.29:2.2: Here, some person has the kind of eye with which one can acquire wealth not yet acquired and increase wealth already acquired,
an3.29:2.3: but he lacks the kind of eye with which one can know wholesome and unwholesome qualities, blameworthy and blameless qualities, inferior and superior qualities, dark and bright qualities with their counterparts.
an3.29:2.4: This is called the one-eyed person.
an3.29:3.2: Here, some person has the kind of eye with which one can acquire wealth not yet acquired and increase wealth already acquired,
an3.29:3.3: and he also has the kind of eye with which one can know wholesome and unwholesome qualities,
an3.29:3.4: blameworthy and blameless qualities, inferior and superior qualities, dark and bright qualities with their counterparts.
an3.29:3.5: This is called the two-eyed person.
an3.29:3.6: “These, bhikkhus, are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world.”

an3.29:4.2: nor does he do deeds of merit;
an3.29:4.3: the blind man destitute of eyes
an3.29:4.4: casts an unlucky throw in both respects.
